questions.stem: A 29-year-old man presents complaining of pain in his left neck and shoulder region following a forced abduction injury to his arm, resulting from a fall from his motorbike at high speed. Subsequent imaging demonstrates an upper brachial plexus lesion. Which of the following nerves is a branch of the lateral cord of the brachial plexus?
questions.explanation: The musculocutaneous nerve is a branch of the lateral cord of the brachial plexus.
questions.source_label: MRCS Part A: 550 SBAs and EMQs || 2nd Edition

questions.stem: A 35-year-old woman presents with winging of the right scapula due to paralysis of the serratus anterior muscle. A lesion to which nerve would result in this presentation?
questions.explanation: The long thoracic nerve supplies serratus anterior; injury causes winging of the scapula.
questions.source_label: MRCS Part A: 550 SBAs and EMQs || 2nd Edition

questions.stem: A 23-year-old man presents following a fall onto his left shoulder whilst playing rugby. He complains of pain throughout the shoulder and has weakness when testing internal rotation of the arm compared to the contralateral side. Injury to which tendon would explain his symptoms?
questions.explanation: Subscapularis is part of the rotator cuff and is responsible for internal rotation of the arm.
questions.source_label: MRCS Part A: 550 SBAs and EMQs || 2nd Edition

questions.stem: A 38-year-old woman presents following a twisting injury during a fall from her horse at low speed. She complains of pain in the region of the fracture and on examination has a wrist drop in the ipsilateral hand. Radiographs reveal a fracture of the humeral diaphysis. An injury to which nerve would explain her presentation?
questions.explanation: The radial nerve runs in the spiral groove of the humerus and is vulnerable in humeral shaft fractures, causing wrist drop.
questions.source_label: MRCS Part A: 550 SBAs and EMQs || 2nd Edition

questions.stem: An 18-year-old man presents following a deep penetrating stab injury to the anterior aspect of his left forearm. Which of the following muscles of the forearm is supplied by the ulnar nerve?
questions.explanation: Flexor carpi ulnaris is supplied by the ulnar nerve.
questions.source_label: MRCS Part A: 550 SBAs and EMQs || 2nd Edition

questions.stem: An 18-year-old man presents with a posterior dislocation of the left elbow. He complains of decreased sensation and weakness throughout the left first web space, and weakness to adduction and abduction of the fingers. Which one of the following nerves has been injured as a result of the dislocation?
questions.explanation: The ulnar nerve supplies the interossei, causing weakness of finger abduction and adduction when injured.
questions.source_label: MRCS Part A: 550 SBAs and EMQs || 2nd Edition

questions.stem: A 48-year-old woman presents with a 1-year history of numbness and tingling affecting the radial three and half digits of her left hand. She has signs of atrophy of the thenar eminence of the hand and has a positive Tinel’s and Phalen’s sign. Compression of which structure is causing the patient’s symptoms?
questions.explanation: Carpal tunnel syndrome is caused by compression of the median nerve beneath the transverse carpal ligament.
questions.source_label: MRCS Part A: 550 SBAs and EMQs || 2nd Edition

questions.stem: A 49-year-old woman has a unilateral mastectomy for carcinoma of the breast. Which of the following is the primary contributor to the arterial supply of the female breast?
questions.explanation: The arterial supply of the breast is mainly from the internal mammary/internal thoracic artery, with contributions from intercostal and axillary branches.
questions.source_label: MRCS Part A: 550 SBAs and EMQs || 2nd Edition
